does: Works garlic with salt in a mortar to a smooth paste, then works in olive oil drop by drop with the pestle, always in one direction, until the paste turns into a thick, pale, glossy sauce. No egg is used: the garlic holds the oil.

intro.what: This alioli works olive oil gradually into a smooth garlic paste in a mortar.
intro.why: It teaches you to build a thick emulsion patiently, waiting for each oil addition to join the paste.

how: Peel the garlic and take out any green shoot, which is bitter. Pound it with a little salt in the mortar until it is a smooth paste with no lumps.
Start turning the pestle in one direction only, and add the oil a drop at a time. Wait until each drop has been taken up before adding more.
As the sauce thickens and turns pale, the oil can go in as a very thin thread. Keep turning the pestle in the same direction.
Stop when the sauce is thick enough to stand up on the pestle. Taste, and add salt or a drop of water if it is too strong.

cues.text: The paste turns from translucent to pale and creamy and stands in soft peaks.
The pestle goes heavy and the sauce clings to the bowl of the mortar.
Sweet and sharp with garlic, with no bitter edge.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the oil too fast, so that the sauce splits into oil and a grainy paste.
mistakes.fix: Add it a drop at a time at first. To mend a split sauce, pound a fresh clove with a little water and work the split sauce into it slowly.

mistakes.mistake: Changing the direction of the pestle, which can undo the sauce.
mistakes.fix: Turn the pestle in one direction only.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the green shoot in the garlic, which tastes bitter.
mistakes.fix: Cut each clove open and take the shoot out.

quiz.question: What is the aim when working oil into garlic?
choices: A separate pool of oil around garlic pieces.
A thin vinegar dressing with coarse garlic.
quiz.because: The garlic paste should hold the oil as a thick sauce rather than leave separate layers.

quiz.question: How should you add oil at the beginning?
choices: In a generous stream before the paste thickens.
All at once, then begin turning the pestle.
Very slowly, waiting for each addition to be taken up.
quiz.because: Slow initial additions give the paste time to take up the oil without splitting.

quiz.question: Which change shows the sauce is developing?
choices: It turns pale and creamy and clings to the mortar.
It becomes grainy with clear oil outside it.
It stays translucent and loose as oil pools.
quiz.because: Paleness, thickness and clinging show the developing sauce rather than separation.

quiz.question: The sauce splits after oil is added too quickly. How would you restart?
choices: Pour in more oil rapidly to thicken it.
Pound fresh garlic with a little water and work the split sauce in slowly.
Keep the same speed and change pestle direction.
quiz.because: A fresh garlic base provides a restart into which the split sauce can be incorporated slowly.

comes_after.why: The sauce starts as garlic pounded smooth with salt in a mortar.

variant_of.differs: A paste of pounded garlic and no egg yolk holds the oil, and the sauce is made by hand in a mortar with a pestle turned one way, slowly. A mayonnaise is whisked in a bowl with egg yolk.
